title: A constant drought correction cut later runoff error at 29 south-east Australian gauges; a rain slope gave no clear added gain
abstract: We tested whether daily-model error fitted in 1997-2009 predicts 2010-2021 runoff beyond a reference correction. We used published annual outputs from fixed GR4J and SIMHYD models at 29 south-east Australian gauges. A constant drought correction reduced later mean squared error by 36.9% (conditional 95% interval 17.5 to 49.4%). Adding a separate rain slope changed error by -0.2% improvement (-52.5 to +22.9%). The line removed pooled bias but gave no added squared-error gain. A constant correction improved scores with AGCD rain, fixed seasonal evaporation and all-pre-1997 calibration. Added slope gains remained uncertain in all variants. We resampled spatial cells and synchronous calendar blocks and refitted drought corrections. Source model and reference fits stay fixed. Earlier controls did not show the same constant gain. This is a retrospective transfer test, not independent field evidence or a diagnosis of a catchment state. Few later years, model structure, shared source errors and untested shrinkage limit the result. Code, aggregate scores, all resampling endpoints and source hashes support reproduction.
